supporting_observations.claim: The periodic HTTPS activity is attributable to C:\Program Files\StockPilot\stockpilotupd.exe (PID 5552), which was launched from the user's Explorer session; the proxy records show connections to update.stockpilot.com.

The updater's connections recur at approximately five-minute intervals: 13:39:21, 13:43:59, 13:49:00, 13:54:25, 13:59:01, 14:04:25, and 14:09:21 UTC. This matches the inventory description of StockPilot checking for updates about every five minutes.
Endpoint network events associate the StockPilot updater with connections to the explicit proxy at each of several checks, corroborating the proxy records' process and destination attribution.
The 13:59:01 check received a proxy 502 gateway error, while other checks received status 200; the recorded error does not by itself indicate malicious activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnels, so the available evidence does not expose the encrypted request or response contents.
The records do not establish whether any update package was downloaded, nor do they provide package-signature or integrity-validation results.
The records support attribution of the listed periodic checks to the StockPilot updater, but do not establish that every connection during the alert window is represented.
claims_not_established: The contents or purpose of the encrypted traffic beyond the recorded destination and connection metadata.
Whether the updater received or installed an update, or whether any update was authentic.
Whether the separate 13:38:32 HTTPS connection to na139.salesforce.com is related to the alert; the available record does not attribute it to the StockPilot updater.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect's VPN UI was launched on WS-EBROOKS-01, followed by a proxy connection to gateway.zscaler.net. Given the supplied context that the organization has no VPN, verify separately whether this software and activity are authorized; this does not explain the alerted StockPilot checks. (T186-00240, T186-00241, T186-00243)

WS-EBROOKS-01 made an SMB connection to FILE-BLU-01 that logged an ANONYMOUS LOGON NTLM network session. Review separately to establish what share or resource was accessed; it is not evidence about the alerted HTTPS activity. (T186-00157, T186-00158, T186-00160, T186-00161)

UserAssist registry entries on WS-EBROOKS-01 record paths corresponding to mstsc.exe and PowerShell. Treat as separate user-activity pivots; these records do not link either program to the alerted connections. (T186-00012, T186-00114)
